Article Title: ‘If you can’t take it back, don’t say it’: Ajay Jadeja’s blunt message to Yashasvi Jaiswal after Asitha Fernando spat
Article Text:
India's Yashasvi Jaiswal, second right, and Sri Lanka's Asitha Fernando (78) exchange words. (AP Photo)

Jadeja warns Jaiswal over physical contact

India coach admits Jaiswal should have kept his distance

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Match referee could decide Jaiswal’s fate

NEW DELHI: Yashasvi Jaiswal ’s heated on-field confrontation with Sri Lanka pacer Asitha Fernando on the opening day of the second Test in Colombo drew criticism from former India all-rounder Ajay Jadeja , who warned the young opener that physical contact crosses a dangerous line.Jaiswal was dismissed for 45 by Fernando in the first session at the SSC ground after the Sri Lankan pacer had conceded three boundaries to the left-hander in the over. Fernando responded with a send-off as Jaiswal began walking back to the pavilion, prompting the India opener to turn around and confront the bowler.The exchange quickly escalated, with the two players trading words before coming face-to-face. Jaiswal’s helmet made contact with Fernando’s forehead, and there was also a push before Sri Lanka captain Dhananjaya de Silva and other players intervened to separate them.Jadeja, speaking on Sony Sports, criticised Jaiswal for taking the confrontation too far and drew a comparison with an earlier incident involving the Indian opener and Sri Lanka’s Niroshan Dickwella."It is dangerous territory. There is no doubt about that. Physical contact is a different thing. In the last match, Jaiswal was on the other side. He was fielding, and he said things to Niroshan Dickwella, and we said that banter is nice as long as there is nothing wrong with your language," Jadeja said on Sony Sports.He then stressed that players who engage in banter must also be prepared to receive it."The same thing happened, but if someone cannot laugh at himself, he shouldn't laugh at others. If you can't take it back, don't say it to others either while standing on the ground," he added.Jadeja's comments came after Jaiswal's confrontation with Fernando turned physical, putting the India batter under the scrutiny of match officials and potentially the ICC Code of Conduct.India batting coach Sitanshu Kotak also acknowledged that Jaiswal should not have moved so close to Fernando, although he suggested the exchange was the result of emotions running high."I think the bowler must have made some comment, and it was probably said in the heat of the moment. Obviously, I don't think Jaiswal should have gone that close, but these things happen in the heat of the moment," Kotak said.Kotak reiterated his assessment in the post-day press conference, saying the exchange could have been triggered by something Fernando said."I think they must have said something to him and it might have happened in the heat of the moment. Obviously, Jaiswal, I don't think he should have been so close (to Fernando), but that happens when you are in the heat of the moment," Kotak said.Sri Lanka fast bowling coach Ryan van Niekerk declined to comment on any possible punishment and left the matter to match referee Andy Pycroft.“The verbals are probably an overflow of emotion. I'll leave that to the match referee to deal with,” he said.Pycroft could examine the incident under Article 2.12 of the ICC Code of Conduct, which deals with “inappropriate physical contact” with another player during an international match.If Jaiswal is found guilty of a Level 1 offence, the possible punishment can range from an official reprimand to a fine of up to 50% of his match fee, along with one or two demerit points.
Article Summary: Match referee could decide jaiswal’s fate after confrontation with asitha fernando. Former india all-rounder ajay jadeja warned the young opener that physical contact crosses a dangerous line. India batting coach sitanshu kotak also acknowledged thatjaiswal should not have moved so close to fernando, but suggested the exchange was the result of emotions running high.

Article Title: Heartbreak for India as Australia advance to semifinals after goalless Hockey World Cup draw
Article Text:
India vs Australia Hockey (Photo by HI)

India push for winner, but Australia hold firm

India’s FIH Women's Hockey World Cup 2026 campaign came to a heartbreaking end as Australia held them to a 0-0 draw and advanced to the semifinals on Sunday. With the result, Australia progressed by virtue of having scored more goals in the pool, while India will now play for fifth place.Australia started strongly and appeared to take the lead in the second minute through Grace Stewart, but India immediately reviewed the goal for dangerous play. The referral went India’s way and the goal was ruled out.The Hockeyroos continued to control possession and created several opportunities, forcing Bichu Devi and Savita into important saves. India also struggled to retain the ball during the opening stages, although they gradually settled into the contest.Australia earned penalty corners but failed to convert, while India’s defence repeatedly managed to clear the danger. The first half ended goalless, despite India earning a penalty corner with just 21 seconds remaining.India came out with greater intensity after the break and began pressing Australia higher up the pitch. However, the Hockeyroos remained dangerous on the counter and continued to test the Indian defence.Australia thought they had finally broken the deadlock in the 40th minute when Kershaw found the net, but another review ruled that the ball had struck an Indian defender’s arm, making the goal illegal.The final quarter became increasingly tense. India created a promising opportunity when Navneet and Lalremsiami found themselves in the centre of the circle but failed to coordinate their attempt.Australia then earned further penalty corners, but India’s first rusher and goalkeeper Bichu Devi stood firm. Colwill’s drag-flick was blocked, while another Australian referral was rejected.With time running out, India removed Bichu Devi and brought on Deepika as an additional outfield player in a final attempt to find the winner. Australia, however, managed the closing stages smartly, keeping possession near the corners and running down the clock.The final whistle confirmed a 0-0 draw. Australia advanced to the semifinals, while India’s hopes of ending their 51-year wait for a World Cup semifinal appearance came to an end.

Tempers were flying high moments after Asitha Fernando dismissed Yashasvi Jaiswal off the last delivery of the 17th over. It was already an eventful over with three boundaries, concluding dramatically when the bowler had the last laugh as Jaiswal inside-edged the delivery back onto his stumps. Disappointed, the left-hander started walking back to the dressing room when something during the animated send-off triggered him, and he instantly returned.The 24-year-old charged toward the bowler, making visible contact with Fernando's head. The Sri Lankan players stepped in, separated the two and prevented the situation from escalating. India's batting coach Sitanshu Kotak felt Jaiswal shouldn't have gone so close and termed the incident as something that happened in the "heat of the moment"."I think the bowler commented something and it happened in the heat of moment. Obviously Yashasvi shouldn’t have gone so close to him but it happened in the heat of the moment," said Kotak.Sri Lanka bowling coach Ryan van Niekerk also downplayed the incident, leaving it to the match referee to deal with."Look it is hard Test cricket, isn't it? When you're coming up against a team like India, you can't sit on the back foot and just bowl at them.I think from our side, it's bringing the challenge all the time, trying to make sure we can create something," said Ryan van Niekerk."And so, from my point of view, I've really asked the bowlers to stand up and create something. The verbals are probably an overflow of emotion. I'll leave that to the match referee to deal with," he added.It now remains to be seen how ICC match referee Andy Pycroft views the incident. Clear video evidence of the physical contact exists and could invite sanctions ranging from a reprimand to a 50% match fee and demerit points. Article 2.12 of the ICC Code of Conduct deals with "inappropriate physical contact"."Inappropriate physical contact with a Player, Player Support Personnel, Umpire, Match Referee or any other person (including a spectator) during an International Match.Note: Any form of inappropriate physical contact is prohibited in cricket. Without limitation, Players will breach this regulation if they deliberately, recklessly and/or negligently walk or run into or shoulder another Player or Umpire.When assessing the seriousness of the breach, the following factors (without limitation) shall be taken into account: (i) the context of the particular situation, including, without limitation, whether the contact was deliberate (i.e. intentional), reckless, negligent, and/or avoidable; (ii) the force of the contact; (iii) any resulting injury to the person with whom contact was made; and (iv) the person with whom contact was made. "

The left-hander started walking back to the dressing room when something during the animated send-off triggered him. The 24-year-old charged toward the bowler, making visible contact with fernando's head.

Article Title: Watch: Max Verstappen’s horrific Dutch GP crash as Lando Norris wins chaotic race
Article Text:
Max Verstappen’s horrific crash (Video grab)

Watch the horrific crash and Hülkenberg’s incredible escape:

Norris keeps title hopes alive

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

A horrific first-lap crash brought Max Verstappen’s Dutch Grand Prix to a premature end on Sunday, with the four-time Formula 1 world champion walking away unhurt after his Red Bull was sent spinning into the barriers in front of his home fans.Verstappen was running seventh when he appeared to lose control while trying to correct a slide through the final corner on the damp track. His car speared into the barrier on the opposite side of the circuit before sliding back across the track and hitting another wall, scattering debris across the racing surface.The dramatic crash immediately brought out the red flag and halted the race. Verstappen, who had started his final Dutch Grand Prix for the foreseeable future, quickly reassured his team over the radio.“I’m OK,” he said, while also apologising to the Red Bull team.The heavy impact forced a delay of around half an hour as marshals cleared Verstappen’s wrecked car and debris from the circuit. The incident also produced another frightening moment moments later.Audi’s Gabriel Bortoleto spun across the track in a cloud of tyre smoke, leaving teammate Nico Hülkenberg with almost no time to react.Hülkenberg made a lightning-quick evasive move to avoid what could have been a huge T-bone collision.“It was crazy with Gabi, I almost T-boned him,” Hülkenberg said over team radio.Verstappen later admitted that he had simply misjudged his speed on the damp surface after rain before the race.The crash proved particularly painful for the Dutch fans, who had turned out in large numbers to cheer their home hero. The Dutch Grand Prix is dropping off the Formula 1 calendar after this season, making Verstappen’s early exit an especially cruel ending to his final home race for now.While Verstappen’s afternoon ended almost immediately, Lando Norris turned the chaotic race into a major boost for his title defence.The McLaren driver started from pole but lost the lead to Mercedes’ Kimi Antonelli at the restart following Verstappen’s crash. Norris gradually reeled him in before making a daring move around the outside of the first corner on lap 54 of 72.He completed the pass and took the lead from Ferrari’s Lewis Hamilton later that lap, holding on despite running on older tyres to secure his second consecutive victory after his Budapest triumph.“This fight is still on,” Norris told his team over the radio after taking the chequered flag.“I knew I was not going to get many chances. Every lap I spent behind him my chances got lower and lower,” Norris said of his decisive move on Antonelli.Antonelli finished second, ahead of teammate George Russell, while Hamilton was fourth. Charles Leclerc was fifth, followed by Oscar Piastri, Liam Lawson, Hülkenberg, Fernando Alonso and Pierre Gasly.Antonelli’s championship lead now stands at 59 points over Russell and Hamilton, while Norris moved into fourth place.
Article Summary: Max verstappen crashes out of dutch grand prix in front of home fans. Red bull driver was running seventh when he lost control on the final lap. Mclaren's lando norris takes second straight victory to keep title hopes alive. Mercedes' kimi antonelli finishes second, ahead of george russell and lewis hamilton.

Article Title: Tom Brady’s Las Vegas Raiders role comes under fire as NFL analyst questions his commitment ahead of 2026 season
Article Text:
Tom Brady faces fresh questions over his Raiders role and commitment. (Image via: Imagn Images)

Tom Brady’s influence has grown, but the Raiders have struggled to turn it into results

Tom Brady’s FOX role keeps the conflict question alive around the Raiders

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Tom Brady’s role with the Las Vegas Raiders is facing fresh questions ahead of the 2026 NFL season. The seven-time Super Bowl champion became a minority owner with a promise of having a major voice in the organization. But after a 3-14 season, another coaching change and a front office shake-up, NFL analyst Mike Florio believes Brady’s divided attention could become a bigger concern.When Brady’s minority ownership was approved, Raiders owner Mark Davis made his expectations clear, saying: “I want Tom to have a huge voice…no question about it.”Brady has since been involved during a major period of change in Las Vegas. The Raiders moved on from general manager Tom Telesco and head coach Antonio Pierce before replacing them with John Spytek and Pete Carroll. Brady was also reported to have played a role in Davis’ decision to make those changes.The results, however, did not match the level of influence surrounding Brady. The Raiders finished the 2025 season at 3-14, the worst record in the NFL, and earned the No. 1 overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft.Carroll then lasted only one season in Las Vegas. Brady also reportedly wanted Ben Johnson to become the Raiders’ head coach, but Johnson ultimately chose the Chicago Bears.That has added another layer to questions about Brady’s influence. Despite the major changes around the team, the Raiders have yet to show that his involvement can produce a clear turnaround.Florio believes the bigger issue is whether Brady can give the Raiders the level of commitment needed to change their direction.“Stop talking about the (Tom) Brady stuff,” said Florio. “Stop talking about it. He’s not going to make him any better as long as he’s doing all this other s**t. So, let him keep doing what he’s doing. Let him think that he’s in a position to turn this thing around because he’s not. I’m more worried about Matt Ryan, I was told, than I am Tom Brady. Because Matt Ryan loaded up the truck and moved to Atlanta. He’s there. He didn’t try to do both jobs. He’s all in, all the time.”Brady’s work as FOX’s lead NFL analyst has created another issue because of his ownership stake. When the league approved his ownership, restrictions were placed on his access to certain Raiders activities and information because of concerns surrounding his broadcasting role.The conflict became especially visible in September 2025 when Brady was seen wearing a headset in the Raiders’ coach’s booth during a game against the Los Angeles Chargers.Florio also compared Brady’s situation with Troy Aikman, who works as a consultant for the Miami Dolphins, while pointing to Matt Ryan’s decision to leave CBS before joining the Atlanta Falcons as president of football operations.“You got to be all in, all the time to be effective. Now, (Troy) Aikman’s in a different spot because he’s not pretending to be the GM or an owner. He’s just kind of an agent out in the field. He’s a traveling salesman for the Dolphins. But is it a conflict? Yes. Should the NFL have never allowed it? Absolutely. They should never have allowed it. ‘Our team’s afraid of Tom Brady helping the Raiders turn it around.’ They’re not. ”Brady has also acknowledged the Raiders’ disappointing performance, saying: “There’s nobody who did a good job.”As the 2026 season approaches, Brady’s role will remain under close attention. His influence over the Raiders is clear, but the team’s results will ultimately determine whether that influence is helping move the franchise forward.
Article Summary: Tom brady’s role with the las vegas raiders is facing fresh questions ahead of the 2026 nfl season. The seven-time super bowl champion became a minority owner with a promise of having a major voice in the organization.

Article Title: Inspiring story on motherhood: "It's probably the hardest thing I've ever done in my life...it's the most daunting task" - How Donna Kelce navigated the challenges of raising Jason and Travis Kelce
Article Text:
Jason Kelce, Donna Kelce and Travis Kelce (Getty Images)

Donna Kelce’s powerful words about motherhood

Glamour group interview published on October 3, 2024

Raising Jason and Travis Kelce was never just about football

Donna Kelce was also building a career

The values behind Jason and Travis Kelce’s success

Why Donna Kelce’s motherhood confession still resonates

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

For Donna Kelce, motherhood was never simply about getting her children through childhood. It meant working hard, making difficult choices and giving Jason and Travis Kelce the freedom to discover who they were. Years before they became NFL stars, she was a working mother trying to keep family life steady. In 2024, she opened up about just how demanding that journey had been.Donna Kelce shared her candid thoughts on motherhood during a. The conversation was part of Glamour’s 2024 Women of the Year feature, which brought together Donna, Tina Knowles, Maggie Baird and Mandy Teefey to discuss raising children who would eventually become major figures in sports, music and entertainment.Asked about what motherhood had been like for her, Donna did not describe it as an effortless or glamorous experience. Instead, she focused on the responsibility that comes with raising children who depend on you for almost everything.She said:“Being a mom is probably the hardest thing I’ve ever done in my life. It’s so much easier to just go to work.”..Donna Kelce then explained that raising children means trying to make the best choices possible while dealing with limited resources and the constant responsibility of caring for people who rely on you.She ultimately described motherhood as the most daunting task she had ever taken on.The honesty in her answer is striking because it came from someone whose sons would later become two of the most recognizable names in American football. Yet Donna was not talking about fame when she made the comment. She was talking about the everyday work of being a mother.That distinction matters.Jason Kelce and Travis Kelce did not begin their childhoods with a clear path toward professional football. Donna told Glamour that the brothers tried several sports, including hockey, lacrosse and basketball. Football came later, when they reached seventh grade.Even then, Donna did not immediately know that her sons would build professional careers from the sport.She said the possibility became clearer only when college recruiting letters began arriving. Until that point, she was simply watching two athletic boys grow, compete and find interests of their own.That detail gives her motherhood comments more weight.The woman who eventually became known around the NFL as “Mama Kelce” was not raising two guaranteed stars. She was raising children without knowing where their talents would eventually take them. Her job was to give them room to grow while keeping them grounded.Donna has also spoken about the energetic nature of her sons as children. During the same Glamour conversation, she recalled broken windows and calls from neighbors, while making clear that Jason and Travis were not bad children. They were simply energetic and, as she put it, rambunctious.Those memories offer a very different picture from the polished image fans now see.Before the Super Bowl appearances, championship celebrations and packed stadiums, there were ordinary family moments. There were mistakes, sports practices, neighborhood adventures and the countless small responsibilities that come with raising children.Another important part of Donna’s story is that motherhood did not happen in isolation.She was also working.Donna had a career in banking and later described herself as a major breadwinner in her family. She told Glamour that she worked extremely hard because she wanted to move forward professionally. At the same time, she believed it was important for her children to see that a woman could build a career and pursue her own ambitions.That balance adds another layer to her comments about motherhood.For Donna, going to work could be demanding, but parenting carried a different kind of responsibility. A job has defined duties, deadlines and hours. Raising children is far less predictable. It follows you home. It changes as children grow. And there is no simple measure for whether you are doing it right.Her reflections also touched on her marriage to Ed Kelce. Donna said the couple knew their marriage was no longer working but chose to remain together for their children for a period of time. She described their relationship as friendly and said they wanted to keep life as normal as possible for Jason and Travis.Eventually, Donna said she had to move forward on her own.That part of her story shows that her definition of motherhood was not limited to the visible moments. It included personal sacrifices and decisions that her sons may not have fully understood while they were growing up.Donna Kelce’s influence becomes easier to understand when looking at how she talks about her sons today.She has consistently emphasized supporting children rather than forcing them into a particular future. In the Glamour interview, she explained that parents learn more about their children as they encounter people and experiences outside their immediate community. Her approach was to support what her children loved and encourage them to enjoy it.That philosophy appears to have shaped the Kelce family.Jason eventually became a Super Bowl champion with the Philadelphia Eagles and one of the most respected centers of his generation. Travis established himself as one of the NFL’s premier tight ends with the Kansas City Chiefs.Their achievements are enormous. But Donna's comments suggest that she measures success differently.For her, keeping her sons grounded mattered just as much as celebrating their accomplishments.She told Glamour that she would remind Jason and Travis of their childhood when fame became overwhelming. The goal was simple: remind them where they came from and help them remember that they were still the same people they had always been.That perspective became especially meaningful as both brothers entered a world where almost every part of their lives could attract public attention.Donna Kelce’s description of motherhood stands out because it cuts through the glamour surrounding her family.Today, Jason and Travis are household names. Their games attract millions of viewers, their personal lives generate constant headlines and their family has become part of the wider sports conversation.But Donna’s story began somewhere much quieter.It began with a mother working, raising two boys and trying to make good decisions without knowing exactly where those decisions would lead.Her statement to Glamour was powerful because she did not present motherhood as a perfect journey. She acknowledged the pressure, uncertainty and sacrifice involved. She also recognized that the work of raising children often happens without applause.That may be the most revealing part of her story.The world sees the Super Bowl rings, the records and the stadium lights. Donna remembers the years before all of that. She remembers the children who needed her, the choices she had to make and the effort required to help them become independent adults.Her famous sons may now be the stars, but Donna’s words offer a reminder that behind many extraordinary careers is a much more ordinary story: a parent showing up, day after day, and doing the best they can.And for Donna Kelce, that was the hardest job of all.
Article Summary: Donna kelce opened up about motherhood during a glamour group interview. She said: “being a mom is probably the hardest thing i’ve ever done in my life. It’s so much easier to just go to work” donna kelce has consistently emphasized supporting children rather than forcing them into a particular future.

Article Title: Inspiring story on mental health: “It’s a big thing for men to be able to talk and speak their feelings and be vulnerable” - How Travis Kelce delivered a powerful reminder that men do not have to suff
Article Text:
Travis Kelce’s powerful message about men and mental health

Kansas City Chiefs training-camp media session in St. Joseph, Missouri, on August 1, 2022

Why Travis Kelce connected vulnerability with brotherhood

Travis Kelce showed that vulnerability can be a form of strength

Travis Kelce’s message still matters beyond the Chiefs locker room

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Travis Kelce has built a reputation around confidence, intensity and leadership. Yet one of his most meaningful messages had little to do with football. In August 2022, the Kansas City Chiefs tight end spoke openly about why men need people they can trust enough to discuss their feelings with. His words offered a reminder that vulnerability does not weaken a man. Sometimes, it is what makes a teammate, brother or friend stronger.Kelce made the remarks during a. KMBC published the comments the following day.The conversation was rooted in football, but Kelce's answer reached far beyond the locker room.He said:“It’s a big thing for men to be able to talk and you know, speak their feelings to, especially to the ones next to them and you know, be vulnerable in those moments.”That short statement carries a surprisingly large message.For years, many men have been taught, directly or indirectly, to hide discomfort. They are often expected to remain calm, tough and in control even when life becomes difficult. Saying that something hurts can feel like admitting weakness. Asking for help can feel even harder.Kelce pushed against that idea.He suggested that men should be able to speak honestly with the people standing beside them.In his world, that means teammates. Outside football, it can mean brothers, friends, partners, coaches or anyone who has earned a person's trust.His point was not that men should constantly talk about their problems. It was that they should not feel ashamed when they need to.The rest of Kelce's answer made his philosophy even clearer. He described emotional openness as part of what it means to be a brother, mentor and good teammate. He also explained that he tries to encourage this kind of supportive atmosphere among the people around him.That idea fits naturally into a professional sports environment.An NFL locker room can be an intense place. Players compete for jobs, deal with injuries, handle public criticism and spend much of their lives under enormous pressure. They are expected to perform even when something outside football is weighing on them.Kelce appeared to understand that a strong team cannot be built only through physical talent.Trust matters. So does friendship.And sometimes, the most important conversation between teammates has nothing to do with the next opponent.Kelce's words suggested that emotional support should not be treated as something separate from leadership. Instead, he viewed it as part of being a responsible teammate. Someone who notices when another person is struggling can offer support before that struggle becomes even heavier.That is a lesson that applies far beyond the NFL.The idea of vulnerability can sound uncomfortable, particularly when discussing professional athletes.Football rewards toughness. Players are praised for playing through pain and maintaining composure under pressure. But emotional strength and emotional silence are not the same thing.Kelce's comments offered a different definition of toughness.Being willing to say, “I'm struggling,” requires honesty. Being willing to listen to someone else requires patience. And creating an environment where another man feels safe enough to open up requires trust.Those qualities do not make someone less strong. They can make relationships stronger.A later mental-health feature from Grow Strong KC highlighted Kelce's remarks in the context of the stigma surrounding men's mental health. The article noted that men can be less likely to seek mental-health treatment and that stigma can become a major barrier to asking for support.That context gives Kelce's 2022 comments even more relevance.He was not presenting himself as a mental-health expert. He was speaking from the perspective of a teammate and leader. His message was much simpler: men should have people they can talk to.Sometimes that is where change begins.What makes Kelce's comments memorable is their lack of drama.He did not deliver a complicated speech. He simply described something he believed mattered.Men need room to talk. They need people who will listen. They need friendships where honesty is not mistaken for weakness.And they need environments where vulnerability does not become a reason for ridicule.Kelce also framed this as part of mentorship. His view was that a good mentor does more than teach someone how to perform. A good mentor helps create an environment where people can become better versions of themselves.That is particularly important for younger athletes.A young player entering professional football may believe that showing emotion will damage his reputation. Seeing an established star speak openly about vulnerability can challenge that assumption.It sends another message: you can be competitive and compassionate. You can be confident and still admit when something is difficult. You can lead without pretending that you have everything figured out.Kelce's comments also fit a broader conversation that has become increasingly important in sports. Athletes are people before they are performers. Their physical health matters, but so does their emotional well-being.The pressure does not disappear simply because someone plays in front of thousands of fans.In fact, fame can create another layer of pressure. That is why having trusted people nearby matters.For Kelce, the answer appeared to be the people beside him. His teammates were not simply colleagues competing for the same championship. They could also be friends, mentors and sources of support.That may be the most powerful part of his message.The NFL star who is known for his loud personality and fearless style was also reminding men that they do not always have to be loud about their struggles.Sometimes, strength looks like opening up. Sometimes, leadership begins with listening. And sometimes, the most important thing a man can say is simply how he feels.
Article Summary: Kansas city chiefs tight end travis kelce spoke openly about why men need people they can trust enough to discuss their feelings with. He suggested that men should be able to speak honestly with the people standing beside them. His words offered a reminder that vulnerability does not weaken a man.

Article Title: How Bangladesh's loss to Australia boosts India's WTC final hopes
Article Text:
L-R: Ajit Agarkar, Gautam Gambhir, Shubman Gill, and Sitanshu Kotak. (PTI Photo)

Bangladesh's loss opens door for India

Bangladesh make ranking history despite defeat

NEW DELHI: Bangladesh's defeat to Australia in the second Test in Mackay has given India a small but significant boost in the race for a place in the World Test Championship (WTC) final.Bangladesh had stunned Australia in the opening Test in Darwin to secure their first-ever Test win Down Under, but Mitchell Starc's 10-wicket match haul inspired the hosts to an innings-and-51-run victory in the second Test on Sunday. The result not only allowed Australia to level the series 1-1 but also cost Bangladesh valuable points in the WTC standings.India, currently fifth in the nine-team table, can now move above Bangladesh and reclaim fourth place by beating Sri Lanka in the second Test in Colombo.Bangladesh remain fourth despite the defeat, but their points percentage (PCT) has dropped sharply from 66.67 after their Darwin victory to 55.56. They now have 50 points from six matches, with three wins, two defeats and one draw.India are just behind them with 64 points and a PCT of 53.33 from 10 matches. Shubman Gill's side have five wins, four defeats and one draw.The equation is straightforward for India: a victory over Sri Lanka in Colombo will take them past Bangladesh and into fourth place.Australia strengthened their position at the top with 96 points and an 80 PCT from 10 matches, while South Africa are second with a 75 PCT and New Zealand third with 72.22.Sri Lanka, India's current opponents, are sixth with a PCT of 33.33. England, West Indies and Pakistan occupy the next three positions.India's bigger challenge, however, is that they need to continue winning consistently to stay in contention for the top two positions that ultimately determine the finalists.Bangladesh's Test campaign has still produced a landmark achievement. Despite losing the second Test, they climbed three places to No.6 in the latest ICC Test rankings — their highest-ever position."Of course (reaching No. 6) is good news," Bangladesh captain Najmul Hossain Shanto said after the Mackay defeat. "I am just hearing about it. To reach No 6 in the Test ranking is a huge achievement. It would have been better if we could have played better cricket in this Test match."Shanto also called for Bangladesh to play more frequently in Australia after their first Test series there in 23 years."We are here after 23 years (first Test series in Australia since 2003). It's not easy to compete in this condition against this quality of team. If we are able to come here consistently, then the players can get an idea of playing here. They will have more experience playing in Australia. They can adjust to this kind of condition and play good cricket," he said."It's hard for the players. Probably 90% of the players haven't played here. They don't know how to adjust, how to cope with this kind of condition, and this kind of bowling attack. My request is that we want to play here. We want to play similar kind of conditions consistently, not after 23 or 25 years," he added.
Article Summary: Bangladesh's defeat to australia in the second test in mackay has given india a boost. India can now move above bangladesh and reclaim fourth place by beating sri lanka in colombo. Australia strengthened their position at the top with 96 points and an 80 pct from 10 matches.

Article Title: ‘Unacceptable’: Justin Langer slams two-day Tests after Australia rout Bangladesh
Article Text:
Australia beat Bangladesh in two days. (Pic credit: CA)

Langer blames batting technique

'Bangladesh need more overseas Tests'

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Former Australia opener Justin Langer has slammed the increasing frequency of Test matches ending inside two days, calling the trend “unacceptable” after Australia wrapped up an innings-and-51-run victory over Bangladesh in Mackay on Sunday.Australia needed only 750 balls to complete the second Test, bouncing back from their shock nine-wicket defeat in Darwin to level the two-match series 1-1. The result also marked the third Test involving Australia in their last seven to finish inside two days, raising fresh concerns over the health of the longest format.“Two-day Test matches (are) unacceptable. It's no good for the game for so many reasons. Last year was disappointing for the crowds, for the kids who get to watch their heroes on TV or listen on the radio or get to the ground,” Langer said on SEN Radio.Langer, who played 105 Tests for Australia, also highlighted the financial consequences of matches ending prematurely.“Economically it's a disaster for Cricket Australia who put money into grassroots cricket. And you know we're talking about very well-paid professionals now, and you get tired of hearing ‘Oh it's just the pitches, oh it's the curators, it's the ball moves a bit’,” he said.Bangladesh were bowled out for 64 in their first innings and 95 in their second, while Mitchell Starc claimed 10 wickets in the match. Langer, however, believes the problem goes beyond pitch conditions and points towards shortcomings in batting fundamentals.“I think a lot of it is down to basic batting technique. Take this test match alone. Almost every dismissal has been batters; their front foot has not gone past the front line. It's just basic technique, and it's footwork patterns.“I coach young guys now, and I've just come back from England; there are a couple of batters who are in our Hundred team who are also wanting to become Test players. And you have some hits with them, and you say some things to them which are so basic for us in the game, and their eyes light up like you're teaching them magic for the first time,” he added.Bangladesh captain Najmul Hossain Shanto admitted his side did not produce their best performance but said the series would provide valuable lessons.“Yeah, obviously I think we all know how good they are and, as I said in the press conference, they have been experienced for almost 50, more than 50 years. So yeah, they played, they showed their character, and as the Bangladesh Test team, we didn’t play our best match,” Shanto said.He acknowledged the challenging conditions in Mackay, where extra bounce and movement made batting difficult.“Yeah, obviously I think this is a different condition, and there is a little bit more extra bounce and swing in the air. So it’s challenging for us. But as a team, if we want to go forward, we need to adjust to this condition, and I hope this experience will help going forward,” he said. Shoriful Islam 's 7/48 was a major positive for Bangladesh, while Shanto also praised Taskin Ahmed and Hasan Mahmud.“It’s quite difficult for all the batters. If you look at their batting also, they also struggled and the way Shoriful, Taskin and Hasan bowled, really happy to see them and it’s quite a difficult wicket to bat, to be very honest,” he said.Bangladesh's historic Darwin victory provided a glimpse of their potential, and Shanto called for more exposure overseas.“Yeah, obviously I think it’s a very proud moment as a team, and we showed our character, and we were disciplined, as you mentioned, in the first Test, and we need to be consistent. I believe if we are able to get more chances, similar kind of conditions here, it will help us, and that’s what we want,” he said.“Not long, long term, like 23 years of coming here and playing two Test matches. It’s not easy. So if we have that chance to play every single year, it will help us to improve our game,” he said.
Article Summary: Australia beat bangladesh in two days. Langer blames batting technique for the result. Australia needed only 750 balls to complete the second test. The result also marked the third test involving australia in their last seven to finish inside two days, raising fresh concerns over the health of the longest format.

Article Title: 'There is no point in playing anymore': Karn Sharma, winner of 4 IPL titles, retires from all forms of cricket
Article Text:
Bengaluru: Royal Challengers Bangalore player Karn Sharma during a training session ahead of the Indian Premier League (IPL) 2024 cricket tournament, at M. Chinnaswamy Stadium in Bengaluru. (PTI Photo/Shailendra Bhojak)

A career filled with achievements

Looking ahead

Former India leg-spinner Karn Sharma has retired from all forms of cricket at the age of 38, bringing an end to a career that lasted more than two decades.Sharma played one Test, two ODIs and one T20I for India, with his last international appearance coming in November 2014.“My station has arrived, I am already 38 and I feel there is no point in playing anymore. The more I play, I will occupy the place of a young player in the team. There is no point in staying in playing when you know that India call will never come. So I spoke to my family and friends and they said, it’s the right time,” Sharma told The Indian Express.Sharma made his only Test appearance against Australia in Adelaide in 2014. He later found it difficult to return to the national team as R Ashwin and Ravindra Jadeja became established in India's spin department.Despite that, Sharma looks back at his career with satisfaction. He played 97 First-Class matches, taking 270 wickets, and represented Uttar Pradesh, Railways, Vidarbha and Andhra. He also featured in more than 90 IPL matches for Royal Challengers Bengaluru, Mumbai Indians, Sunrisers Hyderabad and Chennai Super Kings, winning four IPL titles.“God gave me everything which I never dreamt of. When I began to play cricket, my dream was always to play for India and play all three formats for the Indian team.There are very few players who play all three formats. I did all the hard work, gave all I had. Somewhere in destiny it was written that I will play these games and am happy. I want to thank everyone, my family, friends, coaches, trainers, various Ranji and IPL sides.Physios, trainers and groundsmen, all played a part in my career,” he added.Sharma said receiving his India Test cap remains one of the most memorable moments of his career.“Getting a Test cap remains a special place in my heart. It was the best day for sure. Playing for India and learning I got will hold a special place for sure. Everytime I played, I gave it all I had, I always tried to learn and improve. The time has come for me to say goodbye and sign off cap number 283,” he explains.He has no immediate plans after retirement but wants to remain connected with cricket.“I don’t know, it will be hard to say at the moment but I want to give back to the game. If someone needs my help, I will be there. I will be going into my second innings of my life post retirement, will see what opportunities come my way,” he said.

Sharma played one test, two odis and one t20i for india, with his last international appearance coming in november 2014. He played 97 first-class matches, taking 270 wickets, and represented uttar pradesh, railways, vidarbha and andhra.
